themes_detail.label: Lead Hazard Spike in Housing
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints in CD 205 surged to 3 complaints this week, up 700% from the 8-week baseline average of 0.4 complaints per week—a statistically significant spike (z-score: 5.42) emerging this week amid 265 active building permits (146 alterations) that may be disturbing lead paint in older housing stock.
evidence: 3 lead complaints filed this week vs. 0.4-complaint weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% increase, z-score: 5.42)
146 active alteration permits filed in last 90 days—renovations in pre-1978 buildings are a primary lead disturbance vector
Lead is a known neurotoxin with particular risk to children; spike coincides with renovation season
reporting_angles: Interview DOHMH about whether renovation notifications are reaching residents; inspect whether landlords are following EPA lead-safe work practices
Survey families in buildings undergoing alterations about whether they received lead disclosure and remediation notices

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection Team Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints to the Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) exploded to 7 complaints last week, a 1300% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.5 complaints per week (z-score: 13.0)—the most statistically anomalous signal in the district—suggesting a specific, acute housing or building code enforcement issue this week.
evidence: 7 SPIT complaints last week vs. 0.5-complaint weekly average (1300% increase, z-score: 13.0—highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
SPIT handles complex, multi-agency building violations; this spike indicates coordinated enforcement action or major code breach(es) emerged this week
No Reddit or news mentions suggest this is not yet public knowledge
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for SPIT complaint details from last week to identify the building(s) and violation type(s)
Contact HPD press office to understand what triggered the spike and whether residents are at risk

themes_detail.label: Elevator Failures Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints surged to 35 complaints 2 weeks ago, an 88% increase from the 8-week baseline of 18.6 per week (z-score: 2.91), indicating a sustained infrastructure failure pattern affecting access in a district with significant elderly and disabled populations and active building alteration work.
evidence: 35 elevator complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 18.6-complaint weekly average (88% increase, z-score: 2.91)
146 active alterations filed in last 90 days—construction often disrupts elevator service or damages systems
Community board has repeatedly requested expanded senior center and aging services, suggesting aging population dependent on elevator access
reporting_angles: Interview elderly and disabled residents about how elevator outages have affected their mobility and access to services
Investigate whether DOB is inspecting alterations for elevator system impact; check compliance with ADA and Local Law 26 (elevator modernization)

themes_detail.label: For-Hire Vehicle Complaint Spike
themes_detail.summary: For-hire vehicle complaints jumped to 8 complaints 2 weeks ago, a 178% spike from the 8-week baseline of 2.9 per week (z-score: 4.04), suggesting aggressive ride-hailing service operations or enforcement gaps in a residential district with significant noise and parking complaints.
evidence: 8 for-hire vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.9-complaint weekly average (178% increase, z-score: 4.04)
Illegal parking complaints are second-highest 311 category overall (2,428 over 90 days); for-hire vehicles may be contributing
Noise complaints (residential + street/sidewalk = 4,191 total) suggest vehicle congestion and idling as possible cumulative stressors
reporting_angles: Analyze whether surge correlates with new ride-hailing service entry or expansion (e.g., Via, Juno) in CD 205
Interview residents about whether for-hire vehicles are blocking hydrants, double-parking, or idling—complaints that may not be categorized as vehicle-specific

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog & Animal Abuse Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Over the past 2 weeks, unleashed dog complaints spiked 300% (3 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 baseline, z-score: 3.4) and animal abuse complaints doubled to 11 complaints 2 weeks ago (115% increase, z-score: 3.09), suggesting either an emerging animal welfare crisis or growing resident awareness of enforcement gaps.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8-complaint weekly average (300% increase, z-score: 3.4)
11 animal abuse complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 5.1-complaint weekly average (115% increase, z-score: 3.09)
Converging spike suggests either coordinated abuse, inadequate enforcement, or a specific location becoming a hotspot (e.g., park, lot)
reporting_angles: Map the 311 complaints geographically—are they clustered in one park or neighborhood area?
Interview NYPD Animal Cruelty Enforcement and local animal shelter to understand whether they've seen uptick in surrenders or reports; investigate if specific perpetrator(s) are involved
